findings.description: User input is reflected in the HTTP response without proper output encoding, allowing execution of malicious JavaScript.
reproduction_steps: 2. Inject the payload '<script>alert(1)</script>' into the 'name' parameter.
3. Observe the executed JavaScript in the browser.
findings.remediation: Apply context-aware output encoding and sanitize user input.

findings.description: An environment configuration file is publicly accessible, leaking sensitive system data.
reproduction_steps: 1. Send a GET request to the /.env path.
2. Observe the server responds with a 200 OK and the file contents.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to explicitly deny access to dotfiles and sensitive directories.

findings.description: The endpoint does not enforce object-level authorization. A user can access another user's private data by modifying the ID parameter.
reproduction_steps: 1. Authenticate as User A and obtain a session cookie.
2. Send a GET request to the target URL representing User B's profile.
3. Observe that the server returns User B's sensitive data instead of a 403 Forbidden error.
findings.remediation: Implement strict object-level authorization checks validating that the requested ID belongs to the authenticated user's session.
